newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Zaveryukha says harvest under-reported.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Zaveryukha says harvest under-reported.

text.p: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Zaveryukha, in charge of the harvest, told Interfax news agency on Wednesday that official data putting 1996 gross grain output at 74.8 million tonnes were artificially low.

"This inaccuracy of statistical information is explained by the fact that agricultural producers are lowering their indicators for gross grain output and are under-reporting the total volume," he was quoted as saying.
He did not say by how many millions of tonnes farmers had under-reported output.
But Interfax quoted Zaveryukha as agreeing with an estimate made by Arkady Zlochevsky, head of the OGO commodities trading company, that output was probably four million tonnes higher.
Independent specialists have long said actual grain output in Russia is nearly always officially under-reported by several millions of tonnes.
The government said last year's net, drought-hit harvest was officially 63.4 million tonnes, but private sector specialists said actual output was three or four million tonnes higher.
Zaveryukha said he was not worried by Russia's most recent harvest, one of the worst in three decades, and said domestic producers were able to meet demand.
Russian farmers under-report output to win greater subsidies for the next crop year and because they are afraid of being paid late or not at all by the state.
